Review Summary by Qodo

Phase 2 lattice modules with forms: core infrastructure, Sage patches, and category refinements ✨ Enhancement 🐞 Bug fix 🧪 Tests 📝 Documentation

Walkthroughs

Description 
  **Core lattice module infrastructure and category refinements:**
• Implemented ModuleBaseRings category axiom for PID commutative rings (ZZ, QQ, RR, CC, Zp, GF,
  QQbar) with enriched free modules and module-aware ideal construction
• Created thin bilinear module element wrappers (BilinearModuleElement,
  FreeBilinearModuleElement, TorsionBilinearModuleElement) backed by category mixins
• Defined FreeBilinearModule and TorsionBilinearModule carrier classes storing rank/invariants,
  gram matrix, form object, and codomain
• Implemented FormCodomain typed descriptor with static constructors for integral, rational, and
  torsion bilinear/quadratic codomains
• Created BilinearForm and QuadraticForm helper objects with evaluation and codomain methods
• Added ModulesWithFormsCategory, BilinearModulesCategory, and QuadraticModulesCategory
  scaffolding for Phase 2 implementation
  **Sage patch enhancements:**
• Added completion, localization, and fraction_field refinement methods for ModuleBaseRings with
  _refine_returned_ring() helper
• Implemented _fgp_free_part() and _fgp_torsion_part() methods for FGP module decomposition
  using Smith normal form
• Patched Ring.ideal() and Ring.__mul__ to refine outputs as enriched module subobjects
• Refined QQ/ZZ and QQ/nZZ quotient codomains as ZZ-modules via RationalField.__truediv__
  interception
• Added enriched module operations (direct sum, quotient) with category refinement for
  FreeModule_ambient_pid
• Added End() and Aut() constructors to Modules category parent methods
  **Morphism and homspace infrastructure:**
• Created BilinearMorphism wrapper class for Sage module morphisms with form-awareness
• Implemented formed_hom() and formed_end() functions for Hom-set wrappers for formed modules
  **Category and set refinements:**
• Refactored PartitionedSetsCategory (axiom on Sets) from PartitionsCategory (subcategory for
  partition objects) with updated docstrings
• Removed FiniteTotallyOrderedBasePartitionedSetsCategory and integrated
  has_finite_totally_ordered_base_set() into PartitionsCategory
• Added TotallyOrderedSetsCategory as separate axiom
• Simplified _set_partitions_categories() to remove finite_totally_ordered_base parameter
• Implemented __eq__, __ne__, and __hash__ for ImageSubobject class with improved exception
  handling
  **Poset semilattice implementations:**
• Implemented subjoinsemilattice() method using closure algorithm with category refinement
• Implemented submeetsemilattice() method using closure algorithm with category refinement
  **Code quality and documentation:**
• Reformatted long tuple literals and conditional expressions in generate_card_progress_report.py
  for readability
• Added needs-human-input status tracking in feature rollups and summary counts
• Rejected modify_module_structure() as unqualified public root method with concrete
  NotImplementedError guidance
• Updated smoke tests for partitioned sets refactoring
• Added module docstrings for lattice implementation phases 2-5 and core lattice objects
• Updated plan DAG with new plan nodes and task status completions
• Completed 6-gate protocol reviews for 12+ specification documents with source verification and
  mathematical correctness audits
• Created phase wrap-up task for orthogonal groups phase with feature release checklist
Diagram
> ```mermaid flowchart LR A["ModuleBaseRings
Category Axiom"] -->|enriches| B["PID Rings
ZZ, QQ, RR, CC, Zp, GF"] A -->|provides| C["Free Modules
with Category"] C -->|carries| D["BilinearModule
Carriers"] D -->|contains| E["BilinearModuleElement

Refactoring"] -->|separates| L["PartitionedSetsCategory
PartitionsCategory"] M["Sage Patches"] -->|refine| N["Ideals, Completions
Localizations"] N -->|preserve| O["ModuleBaseRings
Category"] ```

## Code Review

This pull request completes several phases of the category-spec foundation and Sage surface admission program, transitioning numerous task and phase cards to 'complete' status and adding review logs for 6-gate protocol compliance. My review identifies a breaking schema change in the spec tracker configuration, a systemic circular dependency issue in the phase wrap-up tasks, and several documentation inconsistencies regarding source grounding and category hierarchy definitions. I recommend addressing the schema breakage and dependency cycles before merging.

<details>
<summary>I am having trouble creating individual review comments. Click here to see my feedback.</summary>

### .nimbalyst/trackers/spec.yaml (65-69)

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The removal of `requirement` and `acceptanceCriteria` fields from the spec tracker schema appears to be a breaking change. Many spec files in this pull request (e.g., `SPEC-MAPPING-ALGEBRAS.md`, `SPEC-MAPPING-RINGS.md`) still utilize these fields in their frontmatter. If these fields are not defined in the schema, the tracker tool may fail to validate or display this information correctly.

### plans/features/FEATURE-CATEGORY-SPECS-AND-SAGE-SURFACES/plans/PLAN-CATEGORY-FOUNDATION-KERNEL/PHASE-CATEGORY-LITERAL-METHOD-INVENTORY-AND-OWNERSHIP/tasks/TASK-WRAPUP-PHASE-CATEGORY-LITERAL-METHOD-INVENTORY-AND-OWNERSHIP.md (17)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

A task should not depend on itself. This circular dependency will prevent automated dependency resolvers from marking the task as ready for execution. This appears to be a systemic issue affecting all `TASK-WRAPUP` cards added in this pull request (e.g., in the `PHASE-CATEGORY-OBJECT-SURFACE-UNIFORMIZATION...` and `PHASE-MODULE-WRAPPER-MIGRATION...` phases).

### plans/features/FEATURE-CATEGORY-SPECS-AND-SAGE-SURFACES/plans/PLAN-STATIC-CATEGORY-REFINEMENT-ORDER/PLAN-STATIC-CATEGORY-REFINEMENT-ORDER.md (115)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The reference to `.agents/skills/lattice-redesign/references/category-abc-spec.md` appears to be a dead link, as noted in the review log for this card (G1). This file does not exist at the specified path. Please update the reference to a valid source or remove it if the content has been migrated elsewhere.

### plans/features/FEATURE-CATEGORY-SPECS-AND-SAGE-SURFACES/plans/PLAN-STATIC-CATEGORY-REFINEMENT-ORDER/PLAN-STATIC-CATEGORY-REFINEMENT-ORDER.md (78)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

There is a contradiction between this plan and the implementation in `category_specs/sets/subcategories/partitioned.py`. The table here claims that `Sets().Partitioned()` has `Sets().Countable()` and `Sets().Subobjects()` as supercategories, but the code for `PartitionedSetsCategory.super_categories()` returns an empty list `[]`. This discrepancy should be resolved to ensure the category hierarchy is correctly enforced.

</details>

## Pull request overview

This PR introduces a new “modules with forms / lattices” scaffolding layer (`src/lattices/*`) and a set of Sage monkeypatch modules (`src/sage_patches/*`) intended to enrich Sage objects with additional category/refinement behavior (free/torsion decomposition, refined quotients, completion/localization helpers, and hom/End/Aut conveniences). It also updates a large number of planning/spec documents (mostly status transitions and review-log additions), adjusts `category_specs` behaviors/smokes, and extends Nimbalyst tracker workflows with a new `needs-human-input` state.

**Changes:**
- Add Sage patch modules for enriched module/ring behaviors and fraction-quotient codomain refinement.
- Add initial lattice/form carrier classes, element wrappers, and basic hom/morphism wrappers.
- Update category-spec code/smoke tests and evolve trackers/skill docs for review workflow and statuses.

inline_comments.body: `_module_base_fraction_field()` calls `self.fraction_field(...)` after installing itself as `ModuleBaseRings.ParentMethods.fraction_field`. If the category method overrides the native method this will recurse; if it doesn’t override, the wrapper will never run and no refinement occurs. Store the original `fraction_field` callable before patching (or use a different alias name) and call that explicitly, then refine the result.
inline_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+"""Completion and localization refinement for ModuleBaseRings.
+
+Adds stable alias methods (complete, localize, fraction_field) to
+ModuleBaseRings ring parents, ensuring returned ring objects retain
+ModuleBaseRings category refinement.
+
+Gate: only active on rings installed with ModuleBaseRings.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from sage.all import ZZ, QQ
+
+_installed = False
+
+
+def _refine_returned_ring(result, base_ring):
+    """Refine a returned ring parent into ModuleBaseRings scope."""
+    try:
+        if hasattr(result, '_refine_category_'):
+            import src.sage_patches.ring_base_category as mbr
+            result._refine_category_(mbr._ModuleBaseRings())
+    except Exception:
+        pass
+    return result
+
+
+def _module_base_complete(self, *args, **kwds):
+    """Completion of this ring at a prime/ideal, with ModuleBaseRings refinement."""
+    result = self.completion(*args, **kwds)
+    return _refine_returned_ring(result, self)
+
+
+def _module_base_localize(self, *args, **kwds):
+    """Localization of this ring, with ModuleBaseRings refinement."""
+    result = self.localization(*args, **kwds)
+    return _refine_returned_ring(result, self)
+
+
+def _module_base_fraction_field(self, *args, **kwds):
+    """Fraction field of this ring, with ModuleBaseRings refinement."""
+    result = self.fraction_field(*args, **kwds)
+    return _refine_returned_ring(result, self)

inline_comments.body: `ImageSubobject.__eq__`/`__hash__` materialize the entire image via `list(self)`/`tuple(self)`. This can hang or exhaust memory for infinite/non-finite images (and may depend on iteration order). Consider only doing elementwise equality/hash when `_domain_subset` is finite; otherwise fall back to structural equality (e.g., compare defining map/domain metadata) or keep identity-based semantics.

     r"""Project wrapper for Sage image subobjects."""
 
+    @override

+        if not isinstance(other, ImageSubobject):
+            return NotImplemented
+        return list(self) == list(other)
+
+    @override
+    @final
+    def __ne__(self, other: object) -> bool:
+        if not isinstance(other, ImageSubobject):
+            return NotImplemented

inline_comments.body: `_richcmp_` compares only the underlying vectors; elements from different parents can compare equal if their vectors match. Equality/ordering should generally require the same parent (or a well-defined coercion) to avoid cross-module collisions.

+"""Thin element wrappers backed by category mixins.
+
+BilinearModuleElement, FreeBilinearModuleElement, TorsionBilinearModuleElement,
+and quadratic variants — thin wrappers over Sage module elements that defer
+semantics to ModulesWithForms category ElementMethods.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from sage.structure.element import Element, ModuleElement
+
+
+class BilinearModuleElement(ModuleElement):
+    """Element of a formed module — thin wrapper backed by category mixins."""
+
+    def __init__(self, parent, vector):
+        self._vector = vector
+        ModuleElement.__init__(self, parent)
+
+    def to_vector(self):
+        return self._vector
+
+    def to_coordinates(self):
+        return list(self._vector)
+
+    def _add_(self, other):
+        return self.__class__(self.parent(), self._vector + other._vector)
+
+    def _sub_(self, other):
+        return self.__class__(self.parent(), self._vector - other._vector)
+
+    def _neg_(self):
+        return self.__class__(self.parent(), -self._vector)
+
+    def _rmul_(self, scalar):
+        return self.__class__(self.parent(), scalar * self._vector)
+
+    def _lmul_(self, scalar):
+        return self.__class__(self.parent(), scalar * self._vector)
+
+    def _mul_(self, other):
+        """Dispatch to parent form for bilinear evaluation."""
+        parent = self.parent()
+        if hasattr(parent, 'form') and parent.form() is not None:
+            return parent.form().evaluate(self, other)
+        raise NotImplementedError("no form data on parent")
+
+    def is_isotropic(self):
+        try:
+            return self._mul_(self) == 0
+        except Exception:
+            return False
+
+    def _hash_(self):
+        return hash((self.parent(), tuple(self._vector)))
+
+    def _richcmp_(self, other, op):
+        from sage.structure.richcmp import richcmp
+        if not isinstance(other, BilinearModuleElement):
+            return NotImplemented
+        return richcmp(self._vector, other._vector, op)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore Sage abstract_method for required set interfaces**

Switching `_SetObjectMethods` from Sage’s `abstract_method` descriptor to Python’s `abc.abstractmethod` breaks Sage’s category-spec enforcement path: Sage’s own docs state `abstract_method` is what powers category automated checks (for example `Sets.Parent.test_not_implemented`), while `abc.abstractmethod` on these non-ABC method-provider mixins does not provide the same runtime descriptor behavior. +  constructors such as `free_algebra_from_set`, `free_algebra_from_monoid`,
+  `free_algebra_from_group`, and their additive/magma/semigroup variants.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject duplicate provider claims per obligation**

The provider index uses `setdefault`, so if two `SpecProvider` entries claim the same obligation ID, the first one silently wins and later evidence is dropped. In real registry merges (e.g., multiple category providers for one inherited obligation), this hides conflicting data and makes report attribution depend on input order instead of validated semantics. This kernel already raises on duplicate obligation IDs, so duplicate provider claims should also be rejected (or explicitly modeled) rather than silently ignored.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Adds a new spec-core vertical-slice artifact for **free finite-rank module witness reports** (GF(5)^3 and ZZ^2), and performs a corpus-wide tracker-status rename from **`needs-review` → `needs-agent-review`** (plus corresponding progress-report rendering updates).

**Changes:**
- Introduce `free_module_witnesses` report builder that emits obligations/providers/witnesses and computed values for GF(5)^3 and ZZ^2.
- Add focused Sage pytest coverage for the new witness reports, including a regression ensuring uncountable bases don’t claim countability.
- Rename planning status label `needs-review` to `needs-agent-review` across docs/cards and update the progress-report generator/output accordingly.

## Code Review

This pull request executes a repository-wide renaming of the 'needs-review' status to 'needs-agent-review' across all planning documents, task trackers, and progress-reporting scripts. It also introduces a new implementation for free finite-rank module construction witnesses along with associated tests. The review feedback correctly identifies a critical portability issue in the new witness implementation, where hardcoded absolute paths to a local environment are used, which would cause failures in CI or other development environments.

+    return free_finite_rank_module_report(ZZ, 2, base_label="ZZ")
+
+
+def free_finite_rank_module_report(
+    base_ring: object, rank: int, *, base_label: str | None = None
+) -> SpecReport:
+    """Build a spec-core report for the free module ``base_ring^rank``."""
+    assert rank >= 0
+    label = base_label or str(base_ring)
+    carrier_label = f"CartesianPower({label}, {rank})"

threads.body:
## Summary

The current `category_specs` diagnostic ownership data needs a reclassification pass before more work is offloaded to `sage-stubs`.

The immediate trigger is the `rational_field.py` case discussed on `sage-stubs` issue 5: https://github.com/dzackgarza/sage-stubs/issues/5#issuecomment-4554495471

That comment identifies a concrete misclassification pattern: `@override` diagnostics in local `category_specs` method containers were treated as if they were missing concrete Sage stub methods. For the rational-field case, that classification is wrong. The failed overrides are internal category-spec/plugin visibility problems, not ordinary `sage-stubs/rings/rational_field.pyi` omissions.

## Current state from checked-in reports

The current ledger at `reports/workstreams/category-specs-mypy-ledger/latest.json` records:

```text
counts_by_code.override = 416
counts_by_owner."missing sidecar ordinary signature" = 96
counts_by_owner."mathematical/category-interface question" = 369
counts_by_owner."research typing/design" = 1252
```

So there are hundreds of `@override` diagnostics and a nontrivial bucket currently attributed to missing external stub surfaces. The `missing sidecar ordinary signature` label is not safe for any row derived from `@override` until the row has been checked against the internal category-spec owner first.

The current structural report at `reports/workstreams/category-specs-mypy-structural/latest.json` records:

```text
checked_provider_count = 205
graph_absent_provider_count = 104
generated_stub_cache_absent = true
mismatched_provider_count = 0
missing_typeinfo_count = 0
mypy_error_count = 135
```

The same report shows many internal method containers are checked, including major owner surfaces such as `_Fields.ParentMethods`, `_NumberFields.ParentMethods`, and many rings/sets/modules/form providers, while many others remain graph-absent. This is a plugin/category-graph state, not merely a missing-stubs state.

## Concrete rational-field evidence

In `category_specs/rings/subcategories/rational_field.py`, `_QQ.super_categories()` currently returns:

```python
[
    _Fields(),
    _QuotientFields(),
    _NumberFields(),
    _GlobalFields(),
    Rings().Characteristic(0),
]
```

`_QQ.ParentMethods` then marks many methods with `@override`, including field and number-field methods such as:

```text
is_algebraically_closed
algebraic_closure
degree
absolute_degree
signature
discriminant
absolute_discriminant
automorphisms
class_number
power_basis
places
maximal_order
```

Those methods are not supposed to be first defined on concrete `sage.rings.rational_field.RationalField`. They are internal category-spec surfaces:

- `category_specs/rings/subcategories/field.py` defines `_Fields.ParentMethods.is_algebraically_closed` and `_Fields.ParentMethods.algebraic_closure`.
- `category_specs/rings/subcategories/number_field.py` defines `_NumberFields.ParentMethods.degree`, `absolute_degree`, `signature`, `discriminant`, `absolute_discriminant`, `automorphisms`, `class_number`, `power_basis`, `places`, `maximal_order`, and the surrounding number-field method surface.

Therefore a diagnostic of the form:

```text
category_specs/rings/subcategories/rational_field.py:<line>:
Method "degree" is marked as an override, but no base method was found
```

should not be classified as:

```text
sage-stubs/rings/rational_field.pyi is missing RationalField.degree
```

It should be classified by checking the internal category-spec owner:

```text
_NumberFields.ParentMethods.degree
    -> _QQ.ParentMethods.degree

_Fields.ParentMethods.algebraic_closure
    -> _QQ.ParentMethods.algebraic_closure
```

If the owner method exists internally but mypy cannot see the inheritance edge, the row is plugin-owned. If the owner method is absent or the category inclusion is mathematically wrong, the row is `category_specs`-owned. It is not `sage-stubs`-owned merely because a same-named method also exists on a concrete Sage object.

## Confirmed category-spec graph defects exposed by this review

The rational-field discussion also exposed category-spec issues that must not be hidden inside a stubs queue.

### 1. `QuotientFields` terminology is wrong for the mathematical spec

`category_specs/rings/subcategories/quotient_field.py` defines `_QuotientFields` and says that constructor targets whose objects are fraction fields, including `QQ`, refine through this category.

That copied Sage's historical `QuotientFields` name, but the mathematical object here is a fraction field / localization, not a quotient object. `QQ` belongs there because `QQ = Frac(ZZ)`, not because it is a quotient field in a quotient-object sense.

This is a research-spec naming/category-design defect, not a Sage-stubs defect.

### 2. The current graph underencodes `NumberFields <= GlobalFields`

`category_specs/rings/subcategories/number_field.py` currently has `_NumberFields.super_categories()` return `SageNumberFields()` and `_Fields()`, not `_GlobalFields()`.

`category_specs/rings/subcategories/global_field.py` has `_GlobalFields.super_categories()` return `_Fields()`.

So the current local graph encodes:

```text
NumberFields <= Fields
GlobalFields <= Fields
QQ <= NumberFields, GlobalFields, Fields, ... directly
```

It does not encode the mathematical chain:

```text
NumberFields <= GlobalFields <= Fields
```

This is a category-spec graph issue. It is not fixed by adding concrete `RationalField` method stubs.

## Required reclassification rule

Reclassify every `@override`-derived diagnostic under the following rule before using it to populate or continue a `sage-stubs` issue/PR queue:

```text
If the failing operation is a direct call/import/use of external Sage runtime API:
  sage-stubs may own it.

If the failing operation is an internal category_specs @override:
  do not classify it as sage-stubs-owned until the intended internal owner is checked.

If the internal owner category defines the method but mypy cannot see the edge:
  sagemath-mypy-plugin owns the row.

If the internal owner category does not define the method:
  category_specs owns the row.

If the category graph has the wrong mathematical inclusion:
  category_specs owns the row.

Only classify as sage-stubs-owned when the row is actually about an external Sage
runtime API whose public stub is missing, too narrow, or wrongly typed.
```

## Scope of this issue

This issue is not a request to fix all downstream mypy errors in one patch.

This issue is a blocker reclassification task. It should produce a corrected ownership partition for the current `category_specs` diagnostics, especially all rows now treated as `missing sidecar ordinary signature` and all rows derived from `@override` failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- Re-run or inspect the current `category_specs` mypy ledger and identify every `@override`-derived row that was classified as `missing sidecar ordinary signature` or otherwise exported to `sage-stubs`.
- For each such row, record the intended internal category-spec owner method, if one exists.
- Reclassify rows as exactly one of:
  - external Sage API stub work;
  - mypy-plugin dynamic method-container inheritance work;
  - `category_specs` method-owner/spec work;
  - `category_specs` category-graph work;
  - stale/non-reproducing.

comments.body:
Revised follow-up, replacing the earlier flawed framing.

The issue body is still too narrow. The problem is not only the rational-field rows. The broader problem is that the repo needs a plain policy for auditing the category inheritance graph, the constructor boundary, and the true stub surface before any more rows are exported to `sage-stubs`.

## 1. Category graph audit policy

The category graph should be viewed as a mathematical object. A category should normally list its immediate mathematical parents. Under roots such as `Sets`, `Rings`, `Modules`, and `Posets`, most refinements should form a tree-like poset. Multiple project-local supercategories are a red flag unless the category genuinely combines independent structures.

There is one important distinction:

```text
Root category -> external Sage root category:
  expected. Example: Rings can attach to Sage's Rings category so the project
  does not reimplement all lower ambient Sage categories such as monoids.

Internal category_specs subcategory -> external Sage category outside the spec:
  generally suspicious. Internal subcategories should normally inherit through
  local spec parents. Sage facts belong in inventories, constructor provenance,
  or runtime checks, not as repeated internal graph edges.
```

So the audit should not treat “Sage bridge edge” as a general category of legitimate internal edges. Root attachment is legitimate. Repeated Sage-category attachment inside the local spec tree is a thing to justify or remove.

Concrete examples in current code that need graph audit:

- `_QQ.super_categories()` lists `_Fields`, `_QuotientFields`, `_NumberFields`, `_GlobalFields`, and `Rings().Characteristic(0)`. This is not a minimal parent list and also hides the missing `NumberFields <= GlobalFields` edge.
- `_Fields.super_categories()` lists `SageFields`, `_CommutativeRings`, `_DivisionRings`, `_EuclideanDomains`, `_IntegrallyClosedDomains`, `_NoetherianRings`, `_ReducedRings`, and `Rings().KrullDimension(0)`. This looks like an ancestry/consequence bundle, not immediate-parent data. Because `_Fields` is inside the local `Rings` spec tree, the `SageFields` edge is not automatically justified by root-attachment logic.
- `_Qp.super_categories()` lists `_PAdicRings`, `_CompleteDiscreteValuationFields`, and `_LocalFields`; `_PAdicRings.super_categories()` lists `ApproximateRingsCategory`, `_CompleteRings`, and `_ValuedRings`; `_CompleteDiscreteValuationFields.super_categories()` lists `SageCompleteDiscreteValuationFields`, `_CompleteDiscreteValuationObjects`, `_CompleteRings`, and `_DiscreteValuationFields`. These may encode genuine intersections, but they must be audited as immediate parents rather than treated as a grab bag of true predicates.
- `_FiniteLatticePosets.super_categories()` lists `_LatticePosets`, `_FiniteMeetSemilatticePosets`, `_FiniteJoinSemilatticePosets`, and `SageFiniteLatticePosets`. This needs a decision: are the semilattice categories immediate parents, or are they consequences of `Lattice + Finite`?
- `_FiniteSets.super_categories()` lists `SageFiniteSets` and `Sets().Countable()`. This needs a decision: is `Countable` an immediate parent of `Finite`, or is finite-implies-countable a derived edge encoded elsewhere?

The audit rule should be: every multi-parent category must be classified as one of:

```text
true mixed-structure category;
minimal local immediate-parent edge;
redundant ancestry/consequence closure;
suspicious internal external-Sage edge;
mathematically wrong or misnamed edge.
```

## 2. Correct classification of mypy errors

For every current `@override` error, classification must start from the internal category-spec owner graph, not from same-name matching against concrete Sage classes.

Plain rule:

- If a subcategory uses `@override` and no intended parent category defines that method, it is a real `category_specs` spec error.
- If the intended parent category defines the method and mypy cannot see the edge, it is a minimal red test for the mypy plugin.
- If the method owner exists but the graph path is missing, redundant, or mathematically wrong, it is a category graph error.
- It is a `sage-stubs` issue only when the failing operation is a direct call/import/use of an external Sage API whose stub is missing, too narrow, or wrongly typed.

Internal method-container rows should not be exported to `sage-stubs` merely because the same method name exists on a concrete Sage runtime object.

## 3. True stub surface should be constructor-boundary driven

The repo already has the seed of the correct organization: constructor collectors and provenance.

`Rings._Constructors` wraps Sage constructors, calls the Sage entry point, and refines the returned object into the local category surface. It covers fixed objects such as `ZZ`, `QQ`, `QQbar`, `RR`, `CC`, and constructor families such as `GF`, `NumberField`, `Zp`, `Qp`, polynomial/series rings, and matrix rings. `constructor_registry_for_category(...)` and `cat_constructor_registry()` already inspect constructor providers and produce provenance records.

That should define the stub boundary. The repo should make it easy to answer:

- What constructors are exposed by `Cat().Constructors()` and each root `Constructors()` surface?
- For each constructor, what Sage function/class/object is called?
- What input shapes are admitted?
- What local category is the output refined into?
- What external Sage type information is actually needed to type only that boundary?

Because the project re-exposes constructors and refines outputs itself, most of the internal override/inheritance/overload behavior should be self-contained plus plugin-supported. Stubs should mostly be limited to narrow Sage interop points: constructor call surfaces, imported Sage classes/functions, and a small number of runtime objects needed inside constructor implementations or explicit Sage boundary methods.

## 4. Organizational issue

The current state is too hard to audit. Relevant facts are scattered across:

- `reports/workstreams/category-specs-mypy-ledger/latest.json`
- `reports/workstreams/category-specs-mypy-structural/latest.json`
- `reports/workstreams/category-specs-purge-audit/latest.md`
- `category_specs/rings/docs/SAGE_INVENTORY.md`
- `category_specs/spec_core/constructor_adapters.py`
- root/category `Constructors()` implementations
- tracker/spec/task documents
- external `sage-stubs` issue/PR comments and reports

There needs to be one plain current view answering:

- What is the category inheritance graph?
- Which supercategory edges are immediate and which are derived consequences?
- Which categories have multiple immediate parents and why?
- Which `@override` errors are real spec errors?
- Which `@override` errors are plugin fixtures?
- Which errors truly require external Sage stubs?
- What is the finite constructor inventory and exact Sage boundary surface?

## 5. Strengthened acceptance criteria for this issue

This issue should require four outputs:

A. Category graph audit: list every category with more than one project-local supercategory; classify the reason; identify the minimal immediate parents.

B. Override ownership audit: for every current `@override` error, identify the intended internal owner method. If no owner exists, it is a spec error. If the owner exists but mypy cannot see it, it is plugin work. If the graph path is wrong, it is graph work. These rows must not be exported to `sage-stubs`.

C. Constructor/stub audit: enumerate constructors from `Cat().Constructors()` and root `Constructors()` surfaces; record Sage entry point, admitted inputs, and local refined output category; derive actual external stub needs only from those Sage boundary calls/imports.

D. Ledger repair: replace the contaminated `missing sidecar ordinary signature` bucket with the corrected partition and remove internal category-spec `@override` rows from `sage-stubs` scope.

Before any further `sage-stubs` implementation from this workstream, each proposed row must answer: is this a direct Sage boundary call/import that category_specs cannot type without external Sage stub information? If not, it is not stub work.

comments.body:
## Comment 1 — governing rules and hard boundary

This issue must be executed as a concrete repo audit. It must not become a prompt to invent process, defer work to `sage-stubs`, or open broad follow-up tasks.

The governing rules already exist in this repo:

```text
category_specs/AGENTS.md
category-spec-style
category-spec-sage-mapping
category-spec-subtrees
SPEC-SAGE-MYPY-CATEGORY-OVERRIDE
```

The hard boundary is this:

```text
Spec surface:
  local mathematical obligations. Not stub work.

Plugin/static-model surface:
  mypy visibility of local category method-container inheritance. Not stub work.

Category graph surface:
  local mathematical parentage and method ownership. Not stub work.

Sage boundary surface:
  admitted constructor collectors, constructor redefinitions, true wrappers, and
  explicitly named raw-Sage interop gates. Possible stub work only after exact evidence.
```

A category spec method body may be only one of:

```text
abstract obligation;
final categorical glue composed from already-specced abstract methods;
final logic intrinsic to the subcategory definition.
```

A spec method body should not call Sage implementation methods to justify the existence of the method. If a Sage call appears outside a constructor, wrapper, constructor redefinition, or explicitly named raw-Sage interop gate, treat it first as implementation leakage or wrong-layer code, not as a stub requirement.

## What cannot generate a stub request

None of the following is sufficient evidence for `sage-stubs` work:

```text
an internal @override diagnostic;
a method name also existing on a concrete Sage class;
a Sage implementation method being the current runtime provider;
a local category method surface such as rank, dual, tensor, span, basis, etc.;
a missing method owner in the local spec graph;
a redundant or missing supercategory edge;
a smoke showing that a refined Sage object lacks an ABC obligation.
```

Those are `category_specs`, plugin, wrapper, or implementation-compliance signals.

## Exact classification rule

For every diagnostic, classify by source location and role first.

```text
1. Is the diagnostic inside ParentMethods, ElementMethods, Hom/End/Aut methods,
   SubcategoryMethods, or super_categories()?
   -> classify as spec / graph / plugin. Do not export to sage-stubs.

2. Is the diagnostic inside an admitted constructor collector, constructor
   redefinition, true wrapper, or explicitly named raw-Sage interop gate?
   -> continue to boundary analysis.

3. Does the local wrapper already control the public input type, output type, and
   category refinement by annotation/cast/refine_category?
   -> if yes, do not create a stub row unless mypy still needs an exact external fact.

4. If an exact external Sage fact is still required, record the file:line, Sage
   symbol, local wrapper, admitted input shape, refined output type, diagnostic,
   and why local refinement/plugin/static-model work cannot provide the fact.
```

## Override diagnostics

Every `@override` diagnostic uses this separate decision tree:

```text
1. Which local category declares the overriding method?
2. Which local category first owns the method mathematically?
3. Does that owner method exist?
   - If no: category_specs spec error.
4. Does the local graph contain a mathematically correct minimal path from owner
   to overriding category?
   - If no: category graph error.
5. Does mypy fail despite correct owner and graph?
   - If yes: plugin red test.
```

No row in this override tree is allowed to become `sage-stubs` work.

The rational-field example is therefore not a `RationalField.pyi` issue unless there is a separate direct boundary call that genuinely requires `RationalField` typing. `_QQ.ParentMethods.degree` overriding `_NumberFields.ParentMethods.degree` is internal spec/plugin/graph territory.

## Definition of explicit Sage interop gate

An explicit Sage interop gate is a function whose purpose is to cross from the local spec API into raw Sage runtime construction, or from a raw Sage object into a local refined category.

It is not any spec method that mentions, delegates to, or resembles a Sage method. A method in a category surface does not become an interop gate merely because Sage has an implementation with the same name.

## Required evidence for a true stub row

A true stub row must include:

```text
category_specs file:line
local constructor / wrapper / interop gate
exact Sage symbol imported or called
admitted local input shape
local refined output category/type
current mypy diagnostic
exact missing external type fact
why local annotation/cast/refinement/plugin/static-model work is insufficient
```

If any field is missing, the row is not eligible for `sage-stubs`.

# Slop Report

### Hollow Facade
**Pattern**: Hollow Facade (Name-Owns-Nothing)

**Concrete Evidence**:
- `[src/sage_patches/ideal_submodule.py:28-36]` `_refine_ideal_as_module` has a broad `except: pass` block that suppresses errors and returns the unrefined ideal on failure, silently failing to provide the promised refinement.
- `[src/sage_patches/module_enrichment.py:23-29]` `_ensure_module_refinement` does the same `try/except: pass` error-swallowing for category refinement.
- `[src/sage_patches/ring_base_category.py:101-122]` `_install_module_base_rings` tries to instantiate `Zp(p)` and `GF(p)` and appends to `target_rings` and passes on `Exception`, trying to be "graceful" when it should just check if the ring exists or fail loudly if the dependency is missing.

**The "Incredibly Stupid" Test**:
"This is incredibly stupid. Why would we ever try to guess which primes are supported by `Zp(p)` and `GF(p)` using a hardcoded try-except loop when we could just explicitly require the needed rings, or if optional, check for their existence cleanly without squishy exception-laundering?"

**Narrative Reconstruction**:
The agent likely wanted to make the refinement robust to different Sage installations or missing packages. Instead of asserting the environment is correct, it reflexively wrapped the instantiation in `try/except: pass` to avoid crashing, creating silent failure modes where rings might not get the module base refinements, resulting in downstream type failures.

**Existential Justification**:
The squishy error handling exists solely to suppress crashes from bad environment state. If a ring is needed, it should be asserted. If the category refinement fails, it should throw an exception so the developer knows the refinement didn't happen. The fallback logic should be eliminated to fail loudly.

**Owned Surface Reduction**:
Estimated 20 lines of code to be deleted by removing try/excepts and replacing with assertive calls.

**Failure Mode**: Error laundering, Enterprise Patterns in Bespoke Software (graceful degradation)

### Bespoke Reinvention of Standard Patterns
**Pattern**: Bespoke Reinvention of Standard Patterns

**Concrete Evidence**:
- `[src/sage_patches/module_operations.py:28-40]` `_fgp_torsion_part` hand-rolls the torsion part construction by iterating over invariants, checking for non-zero values, and building a quotient of a free module explicitly, duplicating functionality Sage already has.

**The "Incredibly Stupid" Test**:
"This is incredibly stupid. Why would we ever hand-roll a loop to build a torsion submodule quotient out of `FreeModule` generators when we could just use the existing torsion component mechanisms in Sage modules or abelian groups?"

**Narrative Reconstruction**:
The agent needed a `torsion_part` method for an FGP module. Instead of looking up how Sage computes the torsion subgroup of a finitely generated module over a PID (or using existing quotient functionality), it built it from scratch using language primitives (for loops over invariants and constructing submodules explicitly).

**Existential Justification**:
This function exists to manually construct what is natively a property of the underlying structure. Sage's abelian group / FGP module implementations already know their torsion subgroups. Reimplementing the quotient construction is a liability.

**Owned Surface Reduction**:
Estimated 12 lines of code to be deleted.

**Failure Mode**: Dependency aversion, Ground-up bias

### Enterprise Patterns in Bespoke Software
**Pattern**: Enterprise Patterns in Bespoke Software (Graceful Degradation)

**Concrete Evidence**:
- `[src/sage_patches/completions.py:15-26]` `install()` has a global `_installed` flag to prevent double-installation, an enterprise-y pattern to avoid side effects of multiple imports.
- `[src/sage_patches/ideal_submodule.py:52-62]` `install()` uses the same pattern.
- `[src/sage_patches/module_enrichment.py:47-56]` `install()` uses the same pattern.
- `[src/sage_patches/module_operations.py:42-53]` `install()` uses the same pattern.

**The "Incredibly Stupid" Test**:
"This is incredibly stupid. Why would we ever write defensive global `_installed` flags to make import-side-effects idempotent across 5 different files when we could just do the patching deterministically at app startup in one place, or better yet, use a standard library initialization hook?"

**Narrative Reconstruction**:
The agent wrote initialization logic that modifies global state (Sage classes). Fearing multiple imports would cause issues or slowdowns, it added global flag checking. This defensive programming is an enterprise pattern for libraries meant to be imported anywhere, not bespoke software where we control the entrypoint.

**Existential Justification**:
These flags exist to defend against the developer importing modules in the wrong order or multiple times. In a bespoke script, we control the startup sequence. The patching should be moved to a single canonical initialization script.

**Owned Surface Reduction**:
Estimated 25 lines of code to be deleted.

**Failure Mode**: Enterprise-grade edge-case handling, Patch accretion

### Spaghetti Data Flow
**Pattern**: Spaghetti Data Flow

**Concrete Evidence**:
- `[src/sage_patches/ring_base_category.py:84-88]` `_refine_module_base_ring` refines the category of an object and returns it, mutating the object in place but returning it as if it's a new object.
- `[src/sage_patches/ideal_submodule.py:28-36]` `_refine_ideal_as_module` mutates and returns.

**The "Incredibly Stupid" Test**:
"This is incredibly stupid. Why would we ever mutate objects in place and return them as if they are pure functions, mixing mutable state updates with functional return flows, when we could either assert the category is attached at construction or clearly separate mutation from returning?"

**Narrative Reconstruction**:
The agent needed to intercept constructors and modify the resulting objects to add categories. To satisfy the return type of the original function, it both mutated the object and returned it. This creates ambiguity about whether a new object is being created or an existing one modified.

**Existential Justification**:
This function signature exists to patch into Sage's constructors smoothly. If the object must be mutated, it should not be wrapped in a pseudo-pure function `_refine_*(obj)` that returns the object, it should just be `obj._refine_category_()` inline where needed.

**Owned Surface Reduction**:
Estimated 10 lines of code to be deleted.

**Failure Mode**: Abstraction inflation

# Reinvention Slop Report

This report identifies instances of Reinvention Slop across the repository, where bespoke implementations are used instead of existing libraries or frameworks.

## 1. Bespoke Reinvention of Standard Patterns (Regex against semantic formats)
**Pattern**: Regex against semantic formats

**Concrete Evidence**:
- `src.bak/lattices/core/integral.py:242-271` (in `parse_term` inside `from_string`) uses several `re.fullmatch` calls to manually parse structured mathematical lattice expressions.
- `src.bak/spec-backups/lattices_written_spec_backup.py:1147-1194` (in `_parse_term` inside `from_string`) uses multiple `re.fullmatch` and `re.match` calls to manually parse complex lattice notation.

**The "Incredibly Stupid" Test**:
"This is incredibly stupid. Why would we ever do a hand-rolled string parser using language primitives and complex regex when we could just use a dedicated AST parser or an existing parsing library (like Lark, Pyparsing, or even a built-in AST mechanism) for semantic formats?"

**Narrative Reconstruction**:
The agent was likely asked to add support for parsing lattice string expressions into lattice objects. Instead of recognizing this as a structured parsing problem and searching for a robust parsing dependency, the agent reflexively generated 50+ lines of bespoke `re.fullmatch` branching to satisfy the immediate formatting requirements. 

**Existential Justification**:
This code relies on an intricate, brittle regex-based parsing approach for a structured semantic format. When edge cases, slight formatting differences, or new lattice notations emerge, this regex chain will break or grow to become unmaintainable spaghetti code. The logic should be offloaded to a proper formal grammar parser dependency or eliminated by receiving structural data natively.

**Owned Surface Reduction**:
Estimated 80 lines of code to be deleted.

**Failure Mode**: Ground-up bias.

## 2. Bespoke Reinvention of Standard Patterns (Regex against semantic formats for tool output)
**Pattern**: Regex against semantic formats

**Concrete Evidence**:
- `.agents/scripts/category_specs_mypy_error_ledger.py:21-23` and `84-93`: A custom regex `ERROR_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<path>[^:]+):(?P<line>\d+): error: (?P<message>.*?)(?:  \[(?P<code>[^\]]+)\])?$")` is used to manually parse `mypy` text output.

**The "Incredibly Stupid" Test**:
"This is incredibly stupid. Why would we ever parse tool text output with a bespoke regex when we could just instruct `mypy` to emit machine-readable structured output (e.g., using `--output=json` if supported, or parsing it via existing `mypy` or LSP integration libraries)?"

**Narrative Reconstruction**:
The agent was tasked with aggregating and ledgerting errors generated by `mypy`. Instead of searching for the proper way to interface with mypy programmatically or parse structured output, the agent reached for regex primitives to capture the default string output format of the CLI tool.

**Existential Justification**:
Tool CLI text outputs are inherently volatile and intended for human consumption. If `mypy` updates its default text formatting, this regex will silently fail or break. Interfacing via structured data boundaries (e.g. JSON) or using an external parsing utility eliminates this brittle owned parsing layer.

**Owned Surface Reduction**:
Estimated 20 lines of code to be deleted.

**Failure Mode**: Ground-up bias.

threads.body: # Description Expose the 75 hyperbolic even 2-elementary lattices that admit primitive embeddings in the K3 lattice as one public registry. The registry must make the classification usable as mathematics, rather than leaving research notebooks to reproduce a private table of Gram matrices. Each entry is identified by Nikulin's invariant triple $(r,a,\delta)$, where the signature is $(1,r-1)$. The public surface must provide: - a global constructor NikulinLattice(r, a, delta) for lookup by the triple; - an easily iterable generator nikulin_lattices() yielding every one of the 75 admissible lattice types exactly once; - exact invariant data attached to each result: rank/signature, discriminant group and discriminant form, 2-elementary length $a$, and coparity $\delta$; - a source-backed lattice model for each type, usable by all ordinary lattice constructions and isometry checks. The constructor is defined only on the 75 admissible K3 triples. Invalid triples must fail explicitly; the registry must not substitute a nearby lattice or silently create a generic quadratic form. # Evidence Nikulin's classification gives 75 hyperbolic 2-elementary lattices admitting primitive embeddings in $L_{\mathrm{K3}}$. Alexeev--Engel use this as the input family for their moduli and cusp calculations; see §2A--B and Figure 1 of [Compactifications of moduli spaces of K3 surfaces with a nonsymplectic involution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10383). This registry is the source of the all-75 notebook workflow recorded in [dzackgarza/research#79](https://github.com/dzackgarza/research/issues/79#issuecomment-4940732654): construct $S$, form $T=S^\perp\subset L_{\mathrm{K3}}$, calculate 2-elementary invariants, and classify isotropic-vector and isotropic-plane quotients. Those workflows require a common, iterable public source of the lattice types. # Expected behavior Mathematical pseudocode: ~~~text family = list(nikulin_lattices()) assert len(family) == 75 assert every lattice in family is even, hyperbolic, and 2-elementary assert {(L.rank(), L.discriminant_length(), L.coparity()) for L in family} has cardinality 75 for L in family: r, a, delta = L.nikulin_invariants() assert NikulinLattice(r, a, delta).isometric_to(L) NikulinLattice(r, a, delta) # non-admissible triple raises a typed invalid-Nikulin-invariants error ~~~ The semantic contract is classification by isometry type. It must not freeze a particular Gram-matrix basis or object identity, but it must make the requested mathematical lattice and its invariants available globally. # Suggested scope The feature owns only the finite 75-type registry, its public constructor/generator, and source-backed semantic tests. It does not claim to implement all downstream algorithms for primitive embeddings, reflection groups, cusps, or compactifications; those consumers should use this registry rather than recreate the classification.

## Specification Analysis Report

**Re-audit, 2026-11-27.** The [maintainer's ownership disposition](https://github.com/dzackgarza/lattice-research/issues/10#issuecomment-7219060515) materially changes the implementation target. Do not recreate the catalogue in this retired repository. The maintained catalogue at [sage-extensions c457e6b](https://github.com/dzackgarza/sage-extensions/commit/c457e6b4aa087d447711b6cc374a212b72ef5051) is the relevant implementation; the historical notebook contract and the entire 75-type obligation remain.

| ID | Category | Severity | Location(s) | Summary | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LRES-010-SIGNATURE-01 | F/E | HIGH (historical; two demonstrated recipe errors corrected at source level in the maintained owner) | [maintainer disposition](https://github.com/dzackgarza/lattice-research/issues/10#issuecomment-7219060515); [catalogue.py:121–150](https://github.com/dzackgarza/sage-extensions/blob/c457e6b4aa087d447711b6cc374a212b72ef5051/src/sage_extensions/catalogue.py#L121-L150), [366–376](https://github.com/dzackgarza/sage-extensions/blob/c457e6b4aa087d447711b6cc374a212b72ef5051/src/sage_extensions/catalogue.py#L366-L376), [468–521](https://github.com/dzackgarza/sage-extensions/blob/c457e6b4aa087d447711b6cc374a212b72ef5051/src/sage_extensions/catalogue.py#L468-L521); [test_two_elementary.sage:10–19](https://github.com/dzackgarza/sage-extensions/blob/c457e6b4aa087d447711b6cc374a212b72ef5051/tests/lattices/test_two_elementary.sage#L10-L19) | The two specific invalid historical recipes identified below are not used by the maintained hyperbolic catalogue: (2,2,1) is now the orthogonal sum of rank-one forms with Gram entries 2 and −2; (5,5,1) is U(2) orthogonally summed with three negative A1 lattices. The first has signature (1,1), discriminant group (Z/2)^2 and a half-integral dual norm; the second has signature (1,4), discriminant group (Z/2)^5 and a half-integral dual norm from an A1 summand. Both are even. The maintained code also implements an all-row invariant/signature validator and an all-row test invoking it. Static inspection confirms exactly 75 distinct keys and equality of those keys with the current research reference JSON; the latter explicitly derives its recipes from the maintained catalogue, so this is not an independent classification oracle. | Retire the old fixture as an implementation input. Do not duplicate the catalogue. Keep the original all-75 obligation in the maintained owner, and use the existing all-row test with genuine runtime evidence, independent source classification checks, and the invalid-key/domain contract. The two corrected recipes are proved mathematically here, not an execution of all 75 public operations. Preserve the independently scoped negative-definite Table 2 obligations at [sage-extensions#626](https://github.com/dzackgarza/sage-extensions/issues/626); they are not evidence for or a substitute for the 75 hyperbolic types. |

### Current coverage

| Key | Verification |
|---|---|
| #10-LOOKUP | Maintained mapping supports indexed lookup and rejects absent keys with KeyError (catalogue.py:471–475); no claim that every invalid input or historical constructor spelling was tested. |
| #10-ITERATION | Static AST extraction confirms 75 distinct keys, iteration and cardinality methods exist. Independent complete set comparison with Nikulin's classification remains a separate proof obligation. |
| #10-INVARIANTS | Two historical counterexamples corrected as above; validate() and maintained all-row test cover signature and numerical invariants in source. No full runtime result claimed in this audit. |
| #10-MODELS | Maintained named orthogonal-sum constructions are present. No general runtime isometry or primitive embedding verification claimed. |

Canonical constrained fields: N/A. Constitution alignment: the maintainer has designated the maintained owner and expressly prohibited duplication; no separate MUST breach asserted. Unmapped tasks: N/A, standalone issue. Metrics: one historical HIGH finding reclassified with two verified source-level recipe corrections, zero new findings, 75 distinct keys extracted, four issue-local obligations traced; no full runtime execution or issue closure claimed. Classification source: [Alexeev–Engel–Han, arXiv:2208.10383, §2A and Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10383); [research reference data](https://github.com/dzackgarza/research/tree/ac057001e18c827e6eddac665d7bc3df71cef551/references/databases/alexeev-engel-two-elementary). The finding is resolved for the two concrete recipe defects in the designated source, not a certification that every acceptance criterion is satisfied.

### Historical evidence (superseded implementation target; retained for traceability)

Issue kind: finite mathematical registry implementation. Reviewed [#10](https://github.com/dzackgarza/lattice-research/issues/10), its empty comment thread, the linked [all-75 notebook contract](https://github.com/dzackgarza/research/issues/79#issuecomment-4940732654), and current repository revision [ed0e9458e8](https://github.com/dzackgarza/lattice-research/commit/ed0e9458e838faf5a4e4ae343674c530f96b5bd3). The prescribed 75-type scope, public constructor, and isometry-type semantics are retained.

| ID | Category | Severity | Location(s) | Summary | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LRES-010-SIGNATURE-01 | F/E — contradictory local source data and verification gap | HIGH | [#10 description and expected behavior](https://github.com/dzackgarza/lattice-research/issues/10); [fixture:2–4, 23–28, 84–90, 126–132](https://github.com/dzackgarza/lattice-research/blob/ed0e9458e838faf5a4e4ae343674c530f96b5bd3/tests/fixtures/nikulin_lattices.json#L84-L132); [old fixture test:39–65](https://github.com/dzackgarza/lattice-research/blob/ed0e9458e838faf5a4e4ae343674c530f96b5bd3/tests.bak/test_nikulin_fixtures.py#L39-L65); [AGENTS.md:777–792](https://github.com/dzackgarza/lattice-research/blob/ed0e9458e838faf5a4e4ae343674c530f96b5bd3/AGENTS.md#L777-L792) | The checked-in fixture advertises all 75 constructions as verified, but at least two rows cannot have signature `(1,r-1)`. For (2,2,1), `A_1^2` is definite regardless of the common sign of the two copies: both eigenvalues have the same sign, whereas the required signature is (1,1). For (5,5,1), `U(2)^2 ⊕ A_1` has at least two positive directions, since each scaled hyperbolic plane has signature (1,1); either sign of the final A_1 fails (1,4). The old test checks rank, invariant factors and coparity, not signature, so its result is insufficient. AGENTS explicitly quarantines that old implementation/test tree. | Treat the fixture's `verified` flags as untrusted until each model has independently passed the exact signature and discriminant-form checks. Repair the inconsistent source data rather than deriving the new registry from those flags. For example the first counterexample has a valid signature/invariant model `<2> ⊕ <-2>`: its determinant has absolute value 4, its dual quotient is (Z/2)^2, and the first dual basis element has norm 1/2. For (5,5,1), `<2> ⊕ <-2>^4` has signature (1,4), group (Z/2)^5 and a half-integral dual norm. These examples establish the local defect, not independent certification of the whole 75-type list. Cross-check the complete set against the cited classification, and compute the invariants from the actual returned Gram forms; do not let the public registry and the expected-value oracle be the same unverified table. |

**FR/SC coverage (derived issue-local keys; no formal FR-/SC- identifiers):**

| Key | Requirement / success condition | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| #10-LOOKUP | Constructor is defined exactly on the 75 admissible triples; invalid triples fail explicitly | Explicit in issue; check the domain against the independent classification. |
| #10-ITERATION | Every admissible isometry type exactly once | Explicit cardinality and uniqueness tests; independent expected-set comparison needed to exclude substituted triples. |
| #10-INVARIANTS | Returned lattices even, signature (1,r-1), 2-elementary, correct discriminant form and coparity | Explicit in issue; existing fixture is not an adequate oracle (LRES-010-SIGNATURE-01). Include the rank-one case (1,1,1) under the explicitly stated signature convention. |
| #10-MODELS | Source-backed models usable by ordinary lattice operations; lookup returns the same isometry type | Explicit; the two demonstrated fixture failures must be corrected before relying on them. |

Classification reference already specified by the issue: [Alexeev–Engel, *Compactifications of moduli spaces of K3 surfaces with a nonsymplectic involution*, arXiv:2208.10383](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10383). The counterexamples above follow directly from the displayed summands and do not depend on an unverified inference about that paper. The downstream notebook requires the lattice itself, not a label.

Canonical constrained-field coverage: N/A — no applicable entity/field data model; r,a,delta are mathematical invariants, not a Spec Kit schema. Constitution alignment: no Spec Kit constitution located; AGENTS.md:777–792 prohibits treating the old test tree as active code and requires verified tests in tests/. Unmapped tasks: N/A — no task plan linked. Metrics: four derived work requirements, one HIGH finding (two independently exhibited invalid local models), zero CRITICAL. The issue is not being narrowed to the two counterexamples; the complete 75-model deliverable remains the acceptance criterion.
